messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test failure and bug report indicate that when initializing a BigFraction with a double value very close to a simple fraction (e.g., 0.5000000001) with a maxDenominator (e.g., 10), an overflow exception is thrown.

The constructor BigFraction(double value, int maxDenominator) delegates to BigFraction(double value, double epsilon, int maxDenominator, int maxIterations) with epsilon = 0 and maxIterations = 100.

Inspecting the detailed constructor, the fraction is constructed using a continued fraction approach calculating terms p and q. The code detects overflow with this condition:
  if ((p2 > overflow) || (q2 > overflow)) {
      throw new FractionConversionException(value, p2, q2);
  }

This is supposed to handle cases when numerator or denominator exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE.

The bug report suggests that if the value is very close to a simple fraction, e.g., 0.5, but the next iteration causes q2 to overflow, it throws the exception instead of returning the previous best approximation that is close enough.

From the loop:
  if ((n < maxIterations) && (abs(convergent - value) > epsilon) && (q2 < maxDenominator)) 
      continue ;
  else stop;

We see that the loop proceeds until q2 >= maxDenominator or convergence within epsilon.

However, the overflow check is inside the loop before checking convergence and maxDenominator.

Thus, if q2 overflows in the next iteration even though the previous iteration fraction is close enough to the input value, the constructor throws FractionConversionException.

In the comment for that block:
  "// in maxDenominator mode, if the last fraction was very close to the actual value"
  "// q2 may overflow in the next iteration; in this case return the last one."

But instead of returning the last fraction, the current code throws an exception on overflow.

Hence, the root cause is that the overflow condition forcibly throws an exception without considering if the previous fraction p1/q1 is sufficiently close to the input value when maxDenominator mode is set.

Fixing this would require catching this overflow condition and returning the last convergent fraction instead of throwing.

The failing test specifically triggers this by using 0.5000000001 with maxDenominator 10, very close to 1/2, causing the overflow-triggering numerator/denominator in the next iteration to throw when it should have returned the previous approximation of 1/2.

Recent bug reports are unrelated.

Therefore, the bug is located in BigFraction(BigFraction(double, double, int, int)) where the handling of overflow in the continued fraction computation is incorrect and does not return the previous closest fraction in maxDenominator mode, instead throwing an exception.

This matches the symptoms described in the bug report and failing test.

# Summary:
- Overflow check throws exception instead of returning last approximation in maxDenominator mode.
- Leads to failing on doubles close to simple fractions with maxDenominator limit.
- Fix needs to return last fraction when next iteration overflows after finding a close enough approximation.
